blocks.text: Two toddlers in a famine-affected region are both malnourished. One is wasted, with loose skin over visible ribs, alert and ravenously hungry. The other has a swollen belly, puffy feet, sparse pale hair and a flaky rash, and is apathetic. They share the same lack of food, yet their bodies have responded in strikingly different ways.

blocks.markdown: Nutritional disease arises from **deficiency** (inadequate intake or absorption of energy, protein, vitamins or minerals) or **excess** (obesity). **Primary** deficiency results from inadequate diet; **secondary** deficiency results from impaired absorption, increased requirement, increased loss or drug interactions.

### Protein-energy malnutrition

**Marasmus** results from a severe deficiency of *total energy* (calories) as well as protein. The child has severe weight loss and **muscle and fat wasting** (below about 60% of expected weight for age by older classifications), a shrunken, 'old man' face, loose skin and no oedema. Appetite is preserved. The body adapts by catabolising its own fat and muscle to provide energy, while visceral protein synthesis, including albumin, is relatively preserved.

**Kwashiorkor** is caused mainly by *protein deficiency with relatively adequate energy intake* (for example a diet of starchy staple after weaning). Features: **generalised pitting oedema** (from hypoalbuminaemia lowering plasma oncotic pressure), a **fatty liver** (reduced hepatic synthesis of apolipoproteins so triglycerides cannot be exported), skin changes (flaky, hyperpigmented rash), hair changes (sparse, depigmented), apathy and irritability, and relative preservation of subcutaneous fat. Immune function is impaired in both conditions, with susceptibility to infections.

blocks.title: Explaining oedema and fatty liver
blocks.prompt: A child on a maize-only diet has swollen legs and a large soft liver. Explain both findings.

steps.text: Diet is low in protein: the liver cannot make enough albumin, so plasma albumin falls.
Plasma oncotic pressure falls, so net filtration at capillaries rises (Starling forces) and fluid accumulates: pitting oedema.
Reduced synthesis of apolipoproteins prevents export of triglycerides as lipoprotein, so fat accumulates in hepatocytes: fatty liver and hepatomegaly.

blocks.answer: Hypoalbuminaemia causes oedema; deficient lipoprotein synthesis causes hepatic steatosis.

blocks.markdown:
### Vitamin deficiency syndromes

Vitamins are classified as fat-soluble (A, D, E, K) and water-soluble (B group and C). Deficiency of each produces a characteristic syndrome.

rows: Impaired rod function, dry conjunctiva, Bitot spots, keratomalacia; squamous metaplasia of epithelia; increased infection
Poor bone mineralisation: bowed legs, rachitic rosary; bone pain and fractures
Deficiency of clotting factors II, VII, IX, X; neonatal haemorrhage
Neuropathy and heart failure; ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, confusion in alcohol misuse
B12 deficiency also causes subacute combined degeneration of the cord; folate deficiency in pregnancy linked to neural tube defects
Defective collagen synthesis: bleeding gums, perifollicular haemorrhage, poor wound healing
blocks.caption: Vitamin deficiencies and their syndromes.

blocks.title: Match the syndrome
blocks.prompt: (a) A man with alcohol dependence is confused, ataxic and has abnormal eye movements. (b) A woman with a maize-based diet has a sun-exposed rash, diarrhoea and confusion. (c) A baby has bowed legs and a beaded rib cage.

steps.text: (a) Triad of confusion, ataxia and ophthalmoplegia in alcohol dependence: thiamine deficiency (Wernicke encephalopathy).
(b) Dermatitis, diarrhoea and dementia ('3 Ds') in maize-dependent diet: niacin deficiency (pellagra).
(c) Poorly mineralised growing bone: vitamin D deficiency (rickets).

blocks.markdown:
### Obesity and its metabolic complications

Obesity is excess body fat, commonly defined by **body mass index (BMI)** of 30 kg/m^2 or above in adults (thresholds may be adjusted for ethnicity). It arises from a chronic imbalance between energy intake and expenditure, with genetic and environmental contributions. Excess visceral adipose tissue secretes free fatty acids and inflammatory cytokines (TNF, IL-6) and alters adipokines, producing **insulin resistance**. Consequences include **type 2 diabetes mellitus**, **dyslipidaemia** (raised triglycerides, low HDL), **hypertension**, **atherosclerosis and coronary disease**, **non-alcoholic fatty liver disease** progressing to steatohepatitis and cirrhosis, obstructive sleep apnoea, osteoarthritis, gallstones and several cancers. The cluster of central obesity, insulin resistance, hypertension and dyslipidaemia is termed the **metabolic syndrome**.

blocks.title: Calculating BMI
blocks.prompt: A man weighs 102 kg and is 1.80 m tall. Calculate his BMI and interpret it.

steps.text: A BMI of 30 or above defines obesity (class I).

items: Visceral fat is more metabolically harmful than subcutaneous fat.
Insulin resistance links obesity to type 2 diabetes, hypertension and fatty liver.
Marasmus is energy deficiency; kwashiorkor is protein deficiency with oedema.
Vitamin A deficiency is a leading cause of preventable childhood blindness worldwide.

blocks.title: Oedema decides
blocks.text: The quickest discriminator is oedema: kwashiorkor has it, marasmus does not. Then add fatty liver and preserved subcutaneous fat for kwashiorkor, and wasting with preserved appetite for marasmus.

points: Marasmus is total energy deficiency with severe wasting and no oedema; kwashiorkor is protein deficiency with oedema, fatty liver and skin and hair changes.
Vitamin deficiencies produce characteristic syndromes, such as rickets (D), beriberi and Wernicke-Korsakoff (B1), pellagra (niacin), scurvy (C) and night blindness (A).
Obesity produces insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidaemia, hypertension, fatty liver, atherosclerosis and increased cancer risk.

questions.stem: A 2-year-old child has generalised pitting oedema, an enlarged fatty liver and sparse depigmented hair. The diet has been mostly cassava porridge. Which diagnosis fits best?
questions.explanation: Oedema, fatty liver and hair changes on a protein-poor, starchy diet point to kwashiorkor. Hypoalbuminaemia explains the oedema.

questions.stem: Why does the liver become fatty in kwashiorkor?

options.text: Reduced synthesis of apolipoproteins impairs export of triglyceride from hepatocytes

questions.correctOptionText: Reduced synthesis of apolipoproteins impairs export of triglyceride from hepatocytes

distractorRationale.b: Intake of fat is not high.

questions.explanation: Protein deficiency reduces production of apolipoproteins needed to package and export triglyceride, so fat accumulates in hepatocytes.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with chronic alcohol dependence presents with confusion, ataxia and nystagmus. Deficiency of which vitamin is responsible?
questions.explanation: The triad of confusion, ataxia and ophthalmoplegia in alcohol misuse is Wernicke encephalopathy, caused by thiamine deficiency.

questions.stem: Perifollicular haemorrhages, bleeding gums and poor wound healing in a man who has eaten no fresh fruit or vegetables for months suggest deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is needed for collagen cross-linking, so deficiency weakens vessel walls and delays healing.

questions.stem: A woman with BMI 34 kg/m^2, waist circumference above the usual threshold, fasting hyperglycaemia, hypertension and raised triglycerides is most likely to have which unifying underlying abnormality?

options.text: Insulin resistance associated with visceral adiposity (metabolic syndrome)

questions.correctOptionText: Insulin resistance associated with visceral adiposity (metabolic syndrome)
questions.explanation: Visceral fat releases free fatty acids and cytokines that cause insulin resistance, which drives hyperglycaemia, dyslipidaemia and hypertension together.

questions.stem: True or false: In marasmus, generalised pitting oedema is a defining feature.
questions.explanation: Oedema is characteristic of kwashiorkor, not marasmus. Marasmus is characterised by severe wasting without oedema.

questions.stem: A woman weighs 84 kg and has a height of 1.60 m. Calculate her body mass index in kg/m^2, to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: BMI = 84 / (1.60^2) = 84 / 2.56 = 32.8 kg/m^2, which is above the usual obesity threshold of 30 kg/m^2. Higher BMI is associated with insulin resistance and other metabolic complications.

questions.stem: A 1.75 m adult has a BMI of 27 kg/m^2. Calculate the mass loss in kg required to bring the BMI to exactly 24 kg/m^2 at the same height, to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: Height squared is 3.0625 m^2. Current mass = 27 x 3.0625 = 82.7 kg, and target mass = 24 x 3.0625 = 73.5 kg, so the required loss is 3 x 3.0625 = 9.2 kg.

questions.stem: Compare kwashiorkor and marasmus in terms of dietary cause, clinical appearance and mechanism of oedema or its absence.
markingGuide: Marasmus: total energy deficiency; kwashiorkor: protein deficiency with relatively adequate energy
Marasmus: severe wasting of fat and muscle, alert, hungry, no oedema
Kwashiorkor: pitting oedema, fatty liver, skin and hair changes, apathy, fat relatively preserved
Oedema due to hypoalbuminaemia reducing plasma oncotic pressure
Fatty liver from reduced apolipoprotein synthesis
questions.explanation: The contrast depends on whether protein or total energy is the main deficit. Albumin levels explain the oedema.

questions.stem: Match four vitamin deficiencies to their clinical syndromes and one key feature of each.
markingGuide: Vitamin D: rickets or osteomalacia with poor mineralisation
Vitamin C: scurvy with defective collagen and bleeding
Vitamin K: bleeding from reduced factors II, VII, IX and X (any four correct matches)
questions.explanation: Each vitamin has a specific biochemical role, which explains its characteristic syndrome.
